payload.choice_traced: The winner (merge --no-commit + path-classified filter + commit; classification by engine-held path rules; milestone commits on the bless window; tag before merge; archive listable from the grant index) traces to the five weighted criteria, each of which carries its requirement lineage: C1 nothing-lost (R6, R11, veto), C2 trunk-clean (R5, high), C3 permanent name (R3, R4, high), C4 no-partial-state (Q1, R2, R8, high), C5 ordinary-mechanics (medium, from the git-maintainer tension). ONE Pugh run is recorded, with the status quo as datum - today's shipped behaviour, not a hypothetical. The datum FAILS two veto criteria (C1: an empty branch closes as success; C3: no tag exists), so the outcome is a disqualification rather than a score. No second run exists and that is recorded as a deliberate strike, not an omission - the eleven enumerated alternatives were each eliminated on a stated failure at M5, so promoting one to be a rival datum would be decision theater.
payload.sensitivity_ruled: VERDICT: robust to weights, vulnerable to environment. No reweighting can flip a result that rests on two veto failures. Two environment worlds can, and both are now RAID tripwires rather than dismissals: se.raid-tags-not-pushed (risk, owner, HIGH - git does not push tags by default, and the tag is now the only handle on the record, so a plain push would ship claims with nothing behind them; mitigation --follow-tags, and it needs to reach the owner because the owner performs every push), se.raid-shallow-clone-loses-record (risk, agent - --depth truncates the record while the tree still looks complete; --filter=blob:none is safe). A third, se.raid-audit-frequency-shifts-the-balance (assumption, owner), records the one accepted cost the design names openly.
payload.matrix_review: KILLER - the baseline reviewed as data. DECOMPOSITION: four elements plus one standing constraint - E1 the milestone lane, E2 the pointer writer, E3 the atomic close, E4 the working place, and F13 (protect the record from erasure) enforced at the git invocation layer over all of them. CLUSTERING: the tear is between the per-bless lane (E1, E2 - cheap, repeated, fires many times) and the once-only atomic close (E3 - safety-critical), and it is justified by failure mode rather than by tidiness: E3 must be able to refuse without ever undoing what E1 already committed. E2 is deliberately NOT folded into E1 despite sharing a lifecycle, because one writes a commit and the other writes a record field, and merging them would make the pointer's correctness depend on the commit succeeding. ALLOCATION: thirteen functions, thirteen allocations, each exactly once; F10 is allocated to the existing grant index rather than to a new element, and that is stated explicitly so the column is not misread as unallocated. INTERFACES: three, each declared at both ends - I1 the tag name (symmetric, both ends derive it from the same deterministic rule, so no coordination is needed and this is the only cross-cluster coupling), I2 the branch state (asymmetric BY DESIGN and in one direction only - E3 reads what E1 wrote and must never write back), I3 the working place (symmetric in naming). No element reaches inside another. No new element was needed at any point in M6's probing, so nothing returns to this gate.
payload.evaluation_recorded: Q1 close atomicity: ADDRESSED, carried by se.adr-tag-before-merge and E3's ordering - every failure point sits before the single trunk-visible write. ONE RESIDUE FLAGGED HONESTLY: the window between merge --no-commit and the commit leaves trunk's index and working tree mid-merge; a crash there does not move HEAD, so recorded history is safe, but the working copy would need a human abort. That is narrower than the scenario claims, so it is recorded as at-risk rather than addressed, and FC5 automates a check on it. The four stakeholder tensions walked: three addressed (reader/auditor, agent/reader, owner/agent), one deliberately unaddressed (auditor vs git maintainer - the record only grows, accepted and recorded as RAID rather than engineered away). Out of scope and stated: reading the withheld record back through an SE surface is i5e, which is exactly why R12 keeps the archive listable meanwhile.
payload.adrs_traced: Every deciding ADR addresses the requirement that forced it: se.adr-close-merge-filter -> R5, R6; se.adr-tag-before-merge -> R3, R4 (and mitigates risk R1); se.adr-milestone-commits-on-branch -> R1; se.adr-event-classification-by-path -> R5; se.adr-grant-index-stays-on-trunk -> R12, and it is the only one adjudicated by the owner rather than the agent, recorded with its condition that the index never grows content. Each carries its rejected options as history and a breaks_if_removed naming a concrete failure, so the why lives once and is not restated at the application sites.
